utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have been told that the Defence has a matter that it wishes to raise before the witness is brought in. I'll hear the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you for allowing me to raise this issue. I was hoping that we can do that in a closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Let us have a closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: A private session will do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. [Interpretation] Yes, it's all right

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration. I'm going to ask the usher to read the declaration to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Good morning, madam.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Madam, could you tell Their Honours your name, please.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Dzenana Sokolovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Ms. Sokolovic, whereabouts did you grow up?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: In Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Where were you living in November of 1994?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: In Bistrik.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: At that time, were you married or were you single?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: I was married.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And I should ask before I proceed. You said that you lived in Bistrik. Is that a part of Sarajevo, a district of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Are you still married?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: No, I am not. I'm divorced.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: In November of 1994, did you have any children?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, two.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Could you tell the Court their names and their ages in November of 1994, please.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Enida was 8; Nermin was 7. Their last name was Divovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I'm going to be asking you some questions about a day in November in 1994 when you were shot and wounded. Before I do that, I'm going to ask you to tell the people in the courtroom how people of different ethnicities and religions got along with each other before the armed conflict began.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they got along normally. There were no problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Did you have friends who were Catholic or Orthodox?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Did you have any problems with Catholic or Orthodox people?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And now I'm going to be asking you some questions about the day on which you were shot. On the 18th of November, 1994, did you leave the place that you were living in Bistrik?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I went to my mother-in-law's to collect some firewood.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Why did you need to go to your mother-in-law's residence in order to collect firewood?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't have firewood at home to make fire for my children.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Was there any reason connected to the war that you had to go and get firewood? Let me ask a different question. How would you normally cook in your residence during times of peace?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: I was using electricity.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Were you able to use electricity during the armed conflict?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: No. It just was there occasionally and then it went off again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Did you use the wood that you were going to your mother-in-law's for to cook food with?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Did you use it -- did you use it to heat your house?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: What part of Sarajevo does your mother-in-law live in?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: She lived in Novo Sarajevo, Hrasna.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: About how far is it, how long does it take to walk from Bistrik to Novo Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I would say some good three or four hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. Especially with children, I would guess.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: What time did you get to your mother-in-law's?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: I got there in the early evening. I spent the night there and then I wanted to go home. I took the firewood with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And I may have misspoke. It was actually the 17th of November that you left to go to your mother-in-law's and the 18th when you came back; am I right?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your son Nermin, did he want to leave your mother-in-law's place on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: No. He was telling me, Mama, let's stay another day, but I told him that we should go, that school was about to begin, and that's how we set off.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And when you set off to return to Bistrik, about what time of day was it that you left your mother-in-law's place?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was about -- I didn't take long to get down from her place. It was around 11 or 12.00, when the first truce was in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned in that answer that a truce was in place. Would you have gone to your mother-in-law's if there had been --

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Would you have gone to your mother-in-law's --

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: I had no idea that the truce was to be enforced. I set off down the Trigovska Street and people were telling me, It's a truce, and that's how I set off with my children. And I reached the railway station and we were walking. There were people around.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just slow that down and take each part of your answer in turn, madam. You knew that -- you say you knew there was a truce because people on the street told you so; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Was there any other way that you knew that there was a truce in effect on the 18th of November?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I saw trams running, so I just assumed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Did trams run outside of cease-fires or did they only run during cease-fires?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Only when the shooting was, the trams would stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Would you have taken the route home from Novo Sarajevo to Bistrik that you did that day if there had not been a cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: No. I would go the roundabout way, around the bakery, the way I had gone with my children.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: At some point on your walk home, did you come to the area of the Holiday Inn and the university's Faculty of Philosophy?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: I was at the first crossing. My girl crossed -- ran across and I stayed behind with Nermin, and I just saw that my boy fell down, and because I would always tell him, Son, when there's shooting, lie down, and I didn't realise that he was wounded until UNPROFOR put him behind the bushes. At that moment I wasn't aware that my little boy was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now, you said that you were at the first crossing. I'm going to show you some photographs and ask you to identify this first crossing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Ms. Case Manager, could we please display the overhead view with the various sniping incidents on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Ms. Sokolovic, on the monitor in front of you, do you see a photograph of part of the city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: I do see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Do you see the yellow building there, quite distinctive, the Holiday Inn?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Do you see a number of red circles, one inside the other?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And are those red circles of anything -- any relation to the location where you and Nermin were shot that day?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now, when you were at that spot, the spot marked with the red circles, were you in territory controlled by the Bosnian Muslims or in territory controlled by the Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: The Serbs were in control because the shots came from Metalka.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: When you say "Metalka," down at the bottom of the photograph, do you see a number of white and red buildings? Down at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And is Metalka one of those buildings?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know exactly where it is. I know that's where the shots came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Right. Now, that's where the shots came from. And is it your testimony that that area was under control of the Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: But now, going back to the place where the red circles are, where you and Enida and Nermin were walking, was the spot where the red circles are under the control of the Bosnian Muslims or of the Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you. I came this way, from over there, and I walked over to the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Yes. And I understand you crossed the road, but I'm asking you, were you in the territory of the Bosnian Muslim army, the Bosnian army, when you did that, when you crossed that road?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: So you were in Bosnian Muslim territory when you were shot?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, who was holding that particular area I really don't know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. It's not very clear to me what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I'm working on it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I am also having this problem, because I assume that the examination-in-chief will follow its usual rules and that our witness has given an answer already, and I'm objecting to the Prosecution using the method of leading questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, you are not to ask leading questions. Some of them have been slightly leading and I have allowed them. But hereafter, since these are issues of contention between the parties, no leading questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In answer to one issue that Ms. Isailovic raised, I don't believe that at this point the witness has answered the question as to whose territory she was in. I think it has been unclear and I will try to clarify it by some non-leading questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Part of the problem for me is when you ask the question, "Were you in Bosnian Muslim territory when you crossed the road," do you mean having crossed the road, was she then in -- no, all right. Well ask it -- put it more clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: We'll get there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Ms. Sokolovic, let me go at it this way: At your house in Bistrik, which sign of the lines, the confrontation lines, were you living on?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, truth to tell, there were our men over there and those others across the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And did you cross the front lines going back and forth to your mother-in-law's house, or did you stay on your side of the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: No. Again, I'm telling you, I don't know. I may have become a bit nervous. As I was heading towards Metalka, there was UNPROFOR, and then the first crossing that I was supposed to cross, I was shot there, where this line is, with my children.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on from there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, but I'd like to ask the witness a question to clarify things. When you speak about crossing, on the screen we see the picture of the site, and at the top of the picture we see the yellow building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And at the right of the picture there's a tall building, a skyrise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the left you see a white building. So what do you mean by crossing? We see several circles on this picture. From what side were you coming? Were you coming from the side of the skyrise to go towards the white building, or from the white building to go towards the skyrise? And what exactly did you cross, the perpendicular road going towards the Holiday Inn? In what direction were you moving, in fact? Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: Is it possible to have some assistance from the usher, maybe, to clarify the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think what we will do is the photograph -- something similar to the photograph on the monitor is on e-court, and perhaps if we call that up, then the witness can mark with the pen, because on this I don't think she can mark with the pen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: So if you give me one moment to identify the photograph and call it up by its ter number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: It should be map number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: It's photograph number 2, Your Honour, and the ter number is 2819.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: I would -- [Interpretation] So I'd like to understand exactly from what side was the witness coming and where was she going, in what direction, because here I see on the left of the picture, there's vacant space and on the right there's a skyscraper that's more or less blue-coloured. We see the Holiday Inn hotel in yellow. Could the witness show us, by pointing with her finger, in what direction she was moving, walking.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We don't have it on the screen. Could the map be put on the screen. Yes, we now have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we didn't see her draw the line. So on the right-hand side there is this blue skyscraper. Now, did she go from left to right or right to left? Was she walking in the direction of the skyscraper or was she walking towards the left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't understand that answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the left. I went left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So she was walking from the skyscraper towards the left, towards the vacant area at the left of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just suggest that we perhaps erase the line - it can be done - and then we could all see the witness draw the line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The line is now erased.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go ahead, Witness. Would you now show us in what direction you were walking on that day.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, when the Prosecutor talks of crossing, does this mean that you crossed the road that is perpendicular to your itinerary, the road leading to the Holiday Inn hotel? Is that the crossroads that you crossed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. This way, I've ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much. And my last question: From the crossroads, were you able to know exactly where the front line was? Was there a front line separating the two armies or was there no front line at that time in that part of the town? Could you not know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Know what? Grbavica was behind Miljitska [phoen], over there to the left. It couldn't have been anybody else but them. That's where I was shot from, the left side. The bullet passed through me and killed the little one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Ms. Sokolovic, as you made your walk back to Bistrik that day, can you tell us, please, what the weather was like.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't really that overcast. It was, you know ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Was there any problem being able to see a few hundred metres?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Does that mean that you could see a few hundred metres without a problem?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: No. You know what, I couldn't because UNPROFOR was there. I wasn't really looking very carefully, to tell you the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, were there leaves on the trees?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Just a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Was it a foggy day?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: As you started to walk across the street, what side of you was Nermin on?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: My right. He was holding onto my jacket.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And where was Enida?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Prosecutor. I think she said -- Madam Witness, could you show which side you had your son on, with your hand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much. To your left side, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: You can sit down again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Witness. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And as you crossed the street, were you shot?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Probably. I didn't stop anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Were you taken to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And the little one remained on the ground after I had been taken away, and I don't know what happened later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And you were taken to the hospital. Was that with a gunshot wound?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now, going back to the photographs --

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't mean to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Going back to the photographs, Your Honour, on the screen, we have this photograph that has been marked by the witness. I'll ask that it be noted for the record that the witness began that line on the left-hand side of the photograph and ended it on the right-hand side of the photograph to indicate her direction of travel. And I'll ask that that image be captured and introduced into evidence with a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Let that be done.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P88, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours, I'd like to go back to the photograph we originally had, the one with the red circles on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Ms. Sokolovic, we're going to move in now --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: -- we're going to move in on that image, we're going to look at what we see when we move in on that image, and when we've looked at it, I'm going to ask you if what you see is a fair and accurate picture of that intersection where you and Nermin were shot on the 18th of November, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Ms. Case Manager, could we do that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now we're going to rotate this photograph through a complete circle, and we're going to ask you to tell us that this was fair and accurate if it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Could you begin rotating, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Please wait until it's all the way around. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Was that a fair and accurate picture of the intersection where you and your son were shot?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will ask that this portion of what we've just seen be introduced into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P89, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Ms. Sokolovic, do you remember speaking with an investigator of the ICTY named Barry Hogan, and having some video taken in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And if we could, Ms. Case Manager, call up Ms. Sokolovic's portion of that video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Before you do that, I wondered whether the witness would be able to pinpoint the precise area or something approximating to the area where she was actually shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is exactly what she does on the next video clip. You will see the investigator have her stand on the very spot so that we can all see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see it. All right, thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Would that be responsive to the Court's concern?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, thanks. Yes, Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the video is going to be suggestive, so I would prefer that the witness show us on a picture the exact location where she and her son were at the time of these shots, because the video is something that was filmed and in which the Prosecution took part. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let me hear your response to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the video itself is not suggestive. You will see the investigator say, Please go and stand where you were when you were shot. He does not say, Is this the spot? He does not indicate to the witness where she should go and stand in any way. You will see the witness, of her own free will and unguided by the investigator, proceed to the spot where she was shot. And for that reason, I believe that the video is not suggestive, the questions posed by the investigator were not suggestive, and I put it that it would be of material assistance to the Court to have this video in evidence in understanding this witness' testimony and the events to which she is testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll see the video, and if, at a particular point, we determine that it is too suggestive, then we will not allow the question to be put.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Ms. Case Manager, could we play that portion of the video that concerns Ms. Sokolovic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: "Investigator: Witness, at this time I would like to ask you to please stand in the location where you were shot on the 18th of November, 1994. "Can you please point in the direction in which you were walking. "And can you please point to where the bullet hit you and where it exited your body. "Could you please point with your right hand to where it hit you and with your -- and then with your right hand to where it left your body. First, where it hit you; second, where it left your body. "Thank you. And could you please point to where your son was walking beside you at that time. "Thank you. And finally, could you please point in which -- in the direction from which you believe the shot came from on that day. "Thank you. This concludes the video of this sniping incident."

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record, I'm not going to move that into evidence at this time. There are a number of interviews on a single DVD, and after each of the witnesses has authenticated it, I'm going to move the -- we'll move the whole DVD into evidence, just so the Court understands where we're proceeding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic, if you have any submissions to make on the video, we'll hear them. If you have any submissions, you may make them right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will present my submissions later, but for the time being, let me say that the location where we saw the witness -- well, there may have been a suggestion to her before we -- the video was taken and it may not exactly correspond to what we saw today. But I'll have to come back to this later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I hear no objections being made at this time, however, and so I take that I may proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed. I know that you're not seeking the admission at this particular time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Because no one witness can authenticate the entire collection, and so we'll do it bit by bit, and after the last one, we'll submit the entire collection into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Ms. Sokolovic, we saw you on the video pointing where the bullet went in and where the bullet came out of you. After the bullet came out of you, where did it go?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. UNPROFOR. And there was a bush there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, madam. Perhaps I wasn't clear. The bullet went in one side of you, came out the other side of you, and then my question is, where did the bullet go.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And then what happened to your son Nermin?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: At that moment the little one fell. It was against his cheek and it came out his head, the bullet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Was that the same bullet that had just passed through you?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the same one. The same one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Before I go on, just one matter. The video we saw of the interview, was that an accurate video of the interview with Investigator Hogan?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: What wounds did you suffer, what injuries did you have, as a result of you yourself being shot?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, believe me, I didn't ask the doctor. I left the hospital on my own volition because my little girl was alone, and I didn't ask anyone for anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Let me ask you a different question, then. Do you still have any effects as a result of being shot on 18 November 1994?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Da.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Could you describe those to the Court, please.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: My complete abdomen was cut. My muscles were damaged; part of the liver. I have terrible pains, especially with the changes of the weather.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: What effect has this had on you psychologically and emotionally, being shot on the 18th of November, 1994?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Psychologically, let me tell you ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Could you tell us, madam.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: I had these internal liver, muscles. I'm a little bit embarrassed to tell you about all this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: How do you feel? What are your feelings as a result of having been shot? That's the question I'm trying to get at now, your emotions, your feelings.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Very bad, very, very bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Since being shot, have you been able to hold a full-time job?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: How do you support yourself?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: I'm just receiving children's allowance. That's what we live on, myself and my two children.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What work did you do before this incident? Would you direct the question to her.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Ms. Sokolovic, before you were shot, what kind of work were you able to do?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: I was cleaning houses, washing windows in other people's houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: As a result of this bullet hitting him, what happened to your son, Nermin?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: They took him down to the morgue. I suppose they buried him afterwards. I only found out about this five or six days later. They were hiding from me the fact that he had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Were you able to go to Nermin's funeral?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: No. They didn't let me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Were you still in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: I tell you, I should have stayed longer, but seven or eight days later I signed my discharge papers because ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges, in just a sentence or two, what kind of a child Nermin was?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: He was a very nice child. It's not because he was mine. And I forgot to say, when we set off, before he was killed, a foreign lady came, patted him on the head and said, I went through the whole of this city but I've never seen a child as cute as this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Since Nermin was killed, have you had another -- a male child?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: I have two boys.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: What are their names?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: The younger one is called Nermin after the late little Nermin, and the other one is called Edim.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Isailovic, this witness has been through a very traumatic incident, and I expect that you will cross-examine her but take that into account.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Just to answer your comment, I must confess that I feel bad, I feel really bad this morning. I'm also a mother. My son is exactly that age, the age of that poor child. But I'm a Defence counsel, this is a criminal proceeding, and we absolutely have to know what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I have other -- I'm continuing in that -- for this, because I have documents that go against what Mrs. Sokolovic is actually stating, and because of that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Then put them. Let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Sokolovic, my name is Branislava Isailovic, I'm an attorney with the Paris bar. I'm extremely sorry for what happened to you and to your son. However, I have to do my own job, as Defence counsel, Defence counsel of General Milosevic, who is charged here with very serious crimes. And he -- and in order to -- we have to establish facts now. And I really apologise ahead of time. This is probably going to be very unpleasant for you, but unfortunately, I'm duty-bound to ask you all these questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we had a technical problem regarding documents. I found a 65 ter document coming from the Prosecution, and with the help of Ms. Jovanovic, my assistant, we did everything that the e-court procedure provided for to make sure that she would obtain these documents today and to make sure that these documents would be uploaded into the system. But we're told today that among all documents that had been called by the Prosecution -- this is document 65 ter 1484; it is an essential document for this Trial Chamber to establish a very important fact. This is 10 minutes before the break, and we have this technical problem. So we were able to obtain a hard copy of this document. We cannot solve our technical problem. We cannot upload this document. It's not in e-court. Time is running, of course, so I don't know what to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If you have a hard copy, then proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only have one hard copy, unfortunately. I don't have extra copies. I wanted to have photocopies made. It is a B/C/S document. It is in B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How long is the document?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's really short. This is a medical report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How many pages?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a longer document, but the portion that we're interested in are four pages. There's just one sentence, actually, that's of interest to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, you should start and we'll deal with that when we come to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll start with another topic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Sokolovic, if I understood you right, in the picture that you were shown, you were on the pedestrian crosswalk when you were actually shot at. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the place you were when the video was actually filmed was different? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't notice. When I watched it, it looked the same to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Sokolovic, when you were at the film -- where the film was actually filmed, did you see a crossing, a zebra crossing?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Is it that zebra crossing, a pedestrian crossing - in B/C/S we call it a zebra crossing - is it that exact one you were at when you were with your son when he got killed and you got injured?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So you're now telling me that when the video was actually filmed, when you were together with Mr. Barry Hogan from the Prosecution, you were not at the same place you were when you were injured; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: You know what, I was a little bit confused. It was a little bit below this white where I was with this man on the video. That's what the place was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So if I can confirm what you just said, let me repeat: The exact place was the zebra crossing that you already mentioned in your statement, in your declaration today.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Your son, were you holding him with your own left hand? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: No. I was carrying a bag and he was holding to my jacket.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. So he was on your left, because earlier we had some problems to figure out where he was -- whether he was on the right or on the left. Can you show me with your hand on which side of you he was.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Okay, fine. Thank you very much. You can sit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please sit. Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Since that was not verbal, could the record reflect the witness indicated her left side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that behind you there was the museum, the building of the -- the revolution building?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Da.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise to refresh all these very painful memories, but throughout all that time, he was holding your jacket, or was he moving around? You said earlier that there was a foreign lady that came close to him. So was he sometimes running around you or was he always holding your jacket?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: The whole time he never left me, and the girl was in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: At any point in time did he turn towards you, or were you all -- both of you were in the same -- looking towards the same direction?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: We walked normally and we talked to each other. My daughter was in front of me. He never left my side.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, but we have a problem. I'm also following the B/C/S version, and in B/C/S she said "He turned towards me," and in the English transcript it says -- and there it says -- and I'm going to ask the question, therefore, to make sure that she would confirm this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Sokolovic, you said earlier in your own language that he would turn around. So was he turning around towards you while you were crossing?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we -- we talked to each other. He would turn around occasionally and then look again in front of him and then turn again.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Sokolovic, another question that is probably very painful. Your son was seven. How tall was he? I guess he was about as tall as your waist; right?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you, yes, up to my waist, not an inch more.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Sokolovic, when exactly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic, may I ask you, is it your case that this incident didn't take place at all?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, absolutely not. I'm just trying to establish, thanks to the documents that I have and thanks to the witness' statement, to figure out -- or to help you establish exactly where the shot might have come from. That's what I'm trying to establish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Sokolovic, on the way you saw UNPROFOR soldiers; is that true?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: How could you recognise these UNPROFOR soldiers?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: When we were walking, there was another lady with us - I can't remember her name at the moment - and she told me it's UNPROFOR. I didn't know, but she told me that UNPROFOR soldiers were standing there. And that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Was this before or after the accident?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: No, I learned that later. I didn't know. There was talk in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: At the hospital, did you talk with physicians or maybe with reporters?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I talked to a journalist, Petar Sharp, something like that. He came to my house as well. He also came to see me in the hospital and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Sokolovic, when exactly did you know that the shots originated from the Metalka building? Who was the first person to mention that word "Metalka"? Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: In the hospital, when I came around, there was talk that I had been hit from Metalka. There were other people who were mentioning this. There was more of that. So they said that the shots had come from Metalka.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Because earlier you told us that on the photographs you couldn't recognise that building, that it doesn't ring any bell. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you, I really don't know this building. I didn't go often to Grbavica. Bistrik and Princip was our main area, and I seldom went there, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Sokolovic, you remember that after what happened there was a police inquiry. You met with policemen, did you?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing it. Believe me, I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Earlier -- I'm going to show you this -- we had documents, a document that we can't display immediately because of technical problems, but after the break, I'll be able to obtain the report of the inquiry in your own language, in B/C/S, and you can take a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would rather not have had to ask all the questions that have to do with this investigation. However, I think it's maybe time for the break? Am I right or am I wrong about the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We still have five minutes until the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very good. Thank you. My assistant is telling me that the technical problem is solved and we now have the document on e-court. We can now display it. Obviously the problem has been solved. Could we please display page 3 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Sokolovic, can you read? You have no problems reading, or do you have any --

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: I can't see it. I don't have my glasses with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, would you grant me leave to read this in B/C/S and then we will get translation from the booth? Documents have -- the interpreters have the document in B/C/S. It's been zoomed in.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you still have problems reading it, Mrs. Sokolovic?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, I can't see it. I can't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, read the B/C/S so then it will be ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Could you please indicate, before reading out, what is the origin of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the origin of the document. This is a document we obtained by the Prosecution when documents were disclosed. It's on the 65 ter list from the Prosecution. I believe that the Prosecution got this document from the Bosnian police. So it's on the exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, madam. I just don't have the exhibit list in front of me, so could you please say what is the nature of the document? Is it a police report, or what is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely. This is a 65 ter document, 1484. This is a police report, the report on a police investigation, which is normally undertaken after this kind of incident from the criminal police. And like here in this -- you always have a report in this kind of incident. On page 3, you have the report where it says "Opis Dogadjaja." So after this incident, the police is stating, and this is at the end of the first phrase --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I didn't realise Ms. Isailovic was going to commence reading the document. Unless this is a prior inconsistent statement by this witness, I object to this witness being impeached with something she did not write and that is not a statement of hers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It can be put to her and it would be for her to say whether she confirms the proposition being put by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this document is -- the next document I will submit is the medical report, you know, after Mrs. Sokolovic's hospital stay, and she can tell us whether -- but this is a document that comes from the Prosecution. This is not my own document. I managed to find it in the Prosecution's exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The fact that it comes from the Prosecution doesn't, in any way, make it admissible. It still has to meet the tests of admissibility. But can you show us on the document something indicating its origin? You referred to the heading, the title, but could I have that translated.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Description of Events."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And is it signed by anybody?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is. On page 4 of this document, in the heading, you see that it is "Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Ministry of the Interior, Security Services Centre Sarajevo, number H05-2, date 19th November, 1994, Official Report." You have the signature of the report compiled by Salko Cerimagic and Sulejman Pilav. These are always the same names that can be found in these documents coming from the Sarajevo police; it's always the same names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll take the break now and deal with this matter when we return.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can I continue with that document that was on the screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We had an objection by the Prosecutor. I'm going to ask him to repeat it and to develop it, to elaborate on it, and then I'll ask you to reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: May I instead withdraw it. I'll withdraw the objection. As I understand, Ms. Isailovic is going to put a proposition to the witness, and I do not object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Proceed, Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I'd like to go back to the page that was displayed on the screen earlier, page 2 -- no, 3, page 3 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In the police report coming from the Sarajevo police, it is stated in the second part of the first sentence that you have here on the screen, under the heading, and if I understood right, Mrs. Sokolovic has a hard time reading, and so -- which is what the Prosecution actually told me, so the interpreter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document on the screen is in B/C/S. There is an English translation, and I wonder if we could have that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. That would be very helpful. Do you have the English translation?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I put forth the translation, if possible, I would suggest a translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have a translation of this document in English. I have hard copies, but I also believe it is in under 65 ter number 1484, and should be in e-court under that number. May I have a moment to double-check the document, Your Honour. I see the registrar --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Even better. That would be even better. We'll display the translation, if we have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is this document in e-court?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have a document in e-court in its original form, which is B/C/S; however, there is no translation attached.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, let us use the hard copy, putting it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the reason why we couldn't find it in the system.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: If I could give the hard copies to the court personnel, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the meanwhile, while the document is circulated, can I continue to ask a few questions to the witness, just to present the document to the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Sokolovic, you met with the police at the hospital; is that true?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Did the policeman tell you where the shots that hit you and your son originated from?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. From Metalka, that's where the shots came from.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand your -- I didn't hear your answer.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: They did. They showed me that the shots had been fired from Metalka. That's what they said.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But the -- did the physicians examine you also at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what hospital this was?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: The Kosevo Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Is it the hospital that's called Klinicki Centar?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to take a look at the document. I know you have difficulties reading, so could you look at page 8 of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, excuse me, sorry to intervene. The English translation that we were provided only has four pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let her identify the passage and we'll see whether it's in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Sokolovic, can you continue? Are you able to continue, go on with this?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: I can continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mrs. Sokolovic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- are you able to continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The story about the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: At the hospital, the policeman told me that the shots had been fired from Metalka building, but they never came again to ask me anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: On the screen, do you recognise this? I know you can't read this document, but do you recognise this document physically? Do you recognise the form that you obtained in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: On this document there are several sheets of paper. You know when you go to the doctors, you get a report, you get a report saying exactly what kind of treatment you underwent. You know this, don't you?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: On page -- I mean, if we could turn two pages down. On this sheet of paper, the bottom of this page, the physician that operated on you, that treated you in that hospital, wrote a report, a report on your injuries, on the injuries that you were operated on. You understand this?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see this document?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, earlier on, but believe me, as I was suffering a lot of pain at that time, I wasn't really able to go through the whole document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to tell you exactly what is written on this document.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: On the bottom of the page I will read in B/C/S, so you can understand, and the interpreters will translate. And the Trial Chamber already has the English translation. "Paramedially to the left, an entry wound is visible, 0.5 centimetres in diameter and bleeding. Paramedially to the right, an exit wound is visible, the surface of the wound being --" I can't really see if it's 2 centimetres or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's not on the translation that we have.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I don't see that either, Your Honour. The ERN numbers are in sequence, but, no, it is not on the translation that we have. This may be a continuation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Sokolovic, you were a bit confused yesterday -- earlier when we asked you what the left and the right was; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So can I actually deduce from this that when people talk about right or left, you're not too sure about where the right is and where the left is. Could you say something in the microphone, please, because when you just nod, it cannot be written on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please explain.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Sometimes, do you have difficulties figuring out what you're really talking about when you mention left or right? Are you sometimes confused?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm a little confused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Docherty. Do you have the documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I have the document in English, Your Honour. I only have the one copy. However, it could be placed on the ELMO and then the English speakers could press the ELMO button and see the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let that be done.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, on this screen we're going to have the translation in English of the document we mentioned, so that all the English speakers can follow exactly what the document is about, and then I'll continue asking questions, Mrs. Sokolovic. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's on the screen now, and this is what you can read: [In English] "Paramedial left, bleeding, and exit point wound to the paramedial right, and bleeding."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Sokolovic, I will now ask you a question on the sensation of pain. On the pain that you experienced when you got hit --

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: To the left.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You say that you were hit and injured. We know that. We have the document that proves this. So earlier, when you described this unfortunate incident, if I can sum it up, you say -- you say that you were on the crossing with your son. Your son was on your left; you showed that to the Chamber. He was turning his head towards you to talk to you and you had felt nothing, but your son had already fallen. That's exactly what had happened.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Da.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: People that were on -- that were there, because your son fell, took you away from that zebra crossing to pull you behind a car. Is that what happened?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I saw that he'd been taken away. I think it was right away in those, what you call those IFOR. I think they took him away because they didn't allow me to turn around. So I didn't know where or how.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Sokolovic, at that very moment, you did not know exactly on which side you were hit; is that true?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: That's true. The left side.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: We know that now because we have the medical report. But at that time of the shot --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, my objection is that counsel is saying that the medical report is showing that the entrance -- the entrance wound was on the left side, and all that the medical report is saying is that the wound was on the paramedial left. And unless counsel can explain what that adjective means, I don't think she can -- I think she overstates the strength of the document by saying that it shows where the wound was. For the Court's information, there are other documents which I intend to use in my re-examination showing that this entrance wound was on the right-hand side, just as the witness testified on direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So right now you're saying that, according to you -- could you tell us exactly which side you were hit? Could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: The left side.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And you're showing your right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The witness did point to her right side.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So I'm back to my question, my earlier -- the question I wanted to ask earlier. When you were hit, you didn't even figure out that you were hit, not right away. So did you know at the time exactly how the bullet went through you, from which side it came from? What exactly did you know about your wound the minute you were hit?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: You know what, nothing at all. I didn't even see the blood because my bag was ...

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please speak slowly so that we can all understand you. I apologise, Mrs. Sokolovic. Could you please speak slowly.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You can continue.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: My bag was there and I didn't feel it, and then there was the bush over there, concealed, where their cars were, and that was the only time I ever saw blood. But I didn't feel anything other than that, until I was beginning to lose consciousness. I fell unconscious. I know the little one was with me.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not get the last portion of the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Could you just repeat the last part of your answer, Mrs. Sokolovic. You say, "I know the little one was with me," and something else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that's what I said. I asked the lady at the hospital about the little one. When I was there I asked her how she was, and she said she's in a safe place, that she had been taken home.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So could you tell us exactly when you knew that you were wounded with this wound, where this bullet had gone through your body? Could you please tell us? Could you please explain this to us.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know something, when I came to in the room upstairs, those other ladies who were with me in that room, they were asking me, and then I heard at that moment -- like, you know, like something hot, someone spilled something hot over me, and that's when I realised that I had been wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Sokolovic, after you were told some things, you talked with the police afterwards.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In the report, which is the document we saw earlier - page 3 of the document, Your Honour; it's a B/C/S document - the policemen state that first your son was shot and the bullet went through his body and then the bullet hit you and injured you. Did you talk to the police about something that would be of the kind?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty is on his feet. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to that question. Counsel misstated the witness' testimony by saying that it was the witness' testimony that the bullet had struck her son first. The witness' testimony was precisely the opposite, that it struck her first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I thought she was referring to the policeman's statement, to the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did, the one that's on the screen. Yes, the statement we have on the screen at the moment. I take the objection of -- Mr. Docherty's objection into account. He is right. So I will reformulate my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: At that very moment when your son fell and when you were injured, did you have any idea of what had happened? Did you have any idea of who got hit first and who got hit second? Did you have any idea about that, when the shot actually occurred?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Docherty, for this objection, which was fully grounded. Now we have the answer. We have the answer that I wanted to obtain.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Sokolovic, you talk about the bushes behind which you were hidden in order to be protected after your son fell; is that true?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I know Sarajevo, a little bit anyway. Is it fair to say -- and maybe we could see the photograph that the Prosecution showed us earlier. This is a 65 ter photograph, 2835. I'm talking about this place that you're familiar with. I mean, you come from Sarajevo. There are a lot of pine trees. These are trees that do not lose their leaves in the winter, in that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the photograph. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But without the photograph, could you tell us a few words about this? Were there bushes?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that all the trees around the museum are always trees that have their leaves, because they're deciduous, conifers?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: I just saw a little of it because I was beginning to lose consciousness, so I wasn't really paying attention. I was just very afraid.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But now you still live in Sarajevo. So when you think about that part of town -- for example, now, before you arrived here in The Hague, is it still green, this place in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Sokolovic, I'm really extremely sorry for what happened to you, and I really want to express all my sincere apologies. You know, as a mother, as a citizen, too, I'm extremely sorry. Maybe I'll be a bit daring, but I'll say it out bluntly: Do you know that the very next day, without your knowing, the photograph of your poor son lying on the ground on this zebra crossing was used for purposes that have absolutely nothing to do with you as a regular citizen of Sarajevo? Do you know that, that this photograph was used?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Don't answer that question. What's the relevance of that, Ms. Isailovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm now really putting my case before the witness, and our case is -- deals with the media -- the use of the situation that was made by the journalists. We believe that facts were deliberately deformed in order to get an impact on public opinion, because public opinion was controlled and the media were always directing their attention in a specific fashion regarding the armed conflict that occurred in Sarajevo and in Bosnia. And this is the relevance of my question and the crucial importance of my question that I've just put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But how does that -- even if that is so, how does that affect the evidence which is before the Chamber and which we have to assess? I mean, if the media in Sarajevo distorted the facts - and I don't know whether that is so - but if that is so, how does that affect the evidence which is presented before the Chamber for us to assess?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we looked at the facts, we obtained evidence which proved that the facts actually occurred, and then you're here to make a judgement. That's your job. My job is to present maybe one other document, which will also be presented through another Prosecution witness that was planned for tomorrow, I think. And by chance, while we were studying the documents that were presented through this other witness, I discovered this photograph, I came across this photograph. I'm hesitating because it's awful. I think here people are playing with people's feelings, and we are here to establish the facts and responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the Trial Chamber has a question following your question, because you're asking our witness here to give a political interpretation of the case that you're putting forward, and our witness is not here to make a political analysis of the situation. What we need here, as Judges, is to know the truth, know exactly what happened during that incident, what were the wounds, who actually shot and which sides the shot came from. This is what we want. This is what you have to help us with, not on the media analysis or the political analysis that you may present to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Judge, I agree with you. I agree with you and therefore I withdraw my question. I got maybe a bit carried over, maybe I got a bit carried over by anger. I'm sorry but I withdraw my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I must object. The photograph in question of the witness' son was on the monitor during that dialogue. The witness is now quite distraught. It should not have been on the monitor. Could we please take a break to allow the witness to compose herself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's very unfortunate. Yes, we'll take a 10-minute break. --- Break taken at 11.32 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm extremely sorry for what happened earlier. Maybe we didn't really do what we should have done regarding this photograph. I feel a bit guilty of inflicting additional pain to Mrs. Sokolovic, and I really didn't want this to happen. I sincerely apologise, and I will deal with this photograph another way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We accept what you have said. Let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Sokolovic, I wanted to discuss this photograph with you, the photograph of the place where the incident happened. This is the photograph that the Prosecution showed you. It's a picture of Sarajevo, the one we have in our atlas. This is photograph number 1, 65 ter number 0617-1144. Earlier you said that it is always that green because of the trees that are planted around the museum. Here, on this photograph -- do you see the photograph on your screen, Mrs. Sokolovic?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You see those circles. This is where the Prosecution actually filmed you. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can you show us where you were when you were hit and when your son fell, very unfortunately?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: This is where the boy was hit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Please use the pen because I will ask this document, once marked, to be tendered. Mrs. Sokolovic, could you please write on the screen with your pen.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: This is where the boy -- [marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Please press harder in order to mark the screen.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Are you absolutely sure?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You're absolutely sure that you were on the sidewalk and not on the zebra crossing?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was a little bit confused when I was talking about this for the first time. I was nervous.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But now you're telling us that you were on the zebra crossing, or were you on the place that you just marked on the screen? Could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Here. I apologise for being a little bit confused. Here, as I've just shown you, is where I and my little boy were when he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please show us, then, where he fell exactly.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: This is where he fell, right next to me, like this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: To be sure that we're -- that we agree, could you tell us once again what direction you were moving in?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: From down here upwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I can't see. You have to indicate that.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]. Towards ...

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Sokolovic, maybe this photograph is not very clear for you. Could you tell us what are the buildings that are on the right-hand side? Maybe the usher could help you show this building on the right. Could you tell us what this building is?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: These were the museums.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I see what the witness is pointing to, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are the museums.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And in front, on the other side?

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
utterances.text: Believe me, at that moment I didn't look around. Believe me, I don't know. I was lost.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Sokolovic, you live in Sarajevo. You still live in Sarajevo, so you know the city.

utterances.speaker: DZENANA SOKOLOVIC
